sources.title: Issue #12 request: task export acceptance criteria
#7 notes on an abandoned export prototype
sources.omission_reason: Historical discussion of an abandoned export prototype; the current rules are read from the specs instead, so it is not a source of authority here.

slices.outcome: A member can download one project's tasks as a CSV file.
An export holds only the tasks its member may read.
Members find the export from the task list and the help page.

outcomes: A member gets one project's tasks as a CSV file that the help page describes.
units.decision_surface: Which task fields the export writes, and in what order.
scope: the export endpoint and its CSV writer for one project
non_goals: no export formats other than CSV
acceptance: the file has a header row and one row per task
each row holds the task's id, title, assignee and due date
each export is logged with the actor, the project and the time
validation: endpoint tests over a fixture project with three tasks
units.rollback: remove the endpoint; nothing links to it until U-3 lands
units.split_rationale: One outcome and one decision surface: the export file. Splitting the writer out would leave an endpoint with nothing to return and a writer with no caller - a non-testable half.

home.evidence: Fixture: the index has no story whose outcome or seam matches this unit.
search: index rows of FT_101 by observable outcome and seam

outcomes: An export holds only the tasks its member may read, filtered by the access-checked task repository.
units.decision_surface: Which access rule filters an exported row.
units.seam: src/reports/csv/rows.ts through the access-checked task repository
scope: access filtering of exported task rows
acceptance: a member who may read two of three tasks gets exactly two rows
an archived task never appears in an export
a project the member cannot open returns no file
validation: fixture tests run by the repository's test script
units.rollback: remove the module, its fixtures and the one test-script entry
units.split_rationale: One outcome - access-filtered rows - over one bounded module. The archived-task rule and the permission rule share the row query, so splitting them would duplicate the query and leave neither half independently provable.

home.evidence: Fixture: the index has no story whose outcome or seam matches this unit.

outcomes: Members reach the export from the task list, and the help page lists it with the other reports.
units.decision_surface: Where the export button lives and how the help page links to it.
units.seam: the task-list toolbar plus the reports help page
scope: the task-list export button and the help-page entry for the export
acceptance: one export button on the task list
the reports help page lists the export with its columns and limits
validation: a UI test clicks the button and receives the file; the help-page link check passes
units.rollback: remove the button and revert the help-page entry
units.split_rationale: One outcome - discoverability - across two surfaces that must agree. Splitting the button from the help entry would ship an export documented nowhere, or documented with no way to reach it.
